task.description:
DESIGN AMENDMENT (a real gap in the original approved design, found live by TEST-DESIGNER's own mix letflow.check.test run, not covered by any of the original design's OQ-1..OQ-6). Read handoffs/WF02-REQ372-20260921/step-03-test-designer.json in full for the exact evidence: mix letflow.check.test on this branch now shows combined 4522 tests, 32 failures (4496/4528 passed), and 31 of the 32 share one root cause -- Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation.field_existence_violations/3 (lib/letflow/definitions/semantic_validation.ex, around line 300-306) flags EVERY {:var, path} reference in a gateway condition as an undeclared-variable violation whenever `declared_fields` (the VariableSchema fetch result) is an EMPTY map -- because Map.has_key?/2 against an empty map is always false. Since VariableSchema registration is optional today and most pre-existing process-definition fixtures across the suite (req207_vortex_test.exs, req208_meridian_test.exs, req206_swiftroute_test.exs, scheduler_req188_test.exs, engine_test.exs, and more) never registered a VariableSchema at all, activate/2's new hard gate now blocks activation for essentially every pre-existing definition that has zero declared fields -- treating 'no schema was ever declared for this process' as 'every referenced field is a typo', which is not the intent of this requirement (REQ-372's own scope is catching a genuinely mis-typed/mis-typed-against reference against a schema the author DID declare, not retroactively demanding every pre-existing process backfill a full VariableSchema before it can activate).

Produce a narrow AMENDMENT to lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md (edit the existing file in place -- add a new subsection under an appropriate existing section, e.g. after S2's type-pair table or as a new S2.x, clearly marked as an amendment with today's date and the reason) deciding and recording explicitly: when the definition's VariableSchema fetch returns EMPTY (zero declared fields registered for this process at all), does Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation.validate/2 (a) skip both violation classes entirely for that definition (return {valid: true, violations: []} unconditionally, since there is no schema to check against), or (b) some other explicit, justified behavior? State your decision and reasoning explicitly -- this is exactly the kind of boundary this requirement's own acceptance criteria (AC3, 'the comparable/non-comparable type-pair table is stated explicitly ... not left implicit') demands be recorded, not left implicit, and it directly determines whether hundreds of pre-existing fixtures keep working. Also state explicitly: does this change interact with or weaken any of the 10 original acceptance criteria (it should not -- AC1-AC6 all describe definitions that DO have a VariableSchema with real declared fields, so exempting the zero-schema case should be fully compatible) -- confirm this in writing. Update the @spec-style description for Letflow.Definitions.SemanticValidation.validate/2 (and field_existence_violations/3 if its signature/behavior changes) to reflect the amendment. This is a signature/behavior-shape amendment only -- no literal Elixir code bodies (same no-implementation-code rule as the original design gate).

You are on branch feature/WF02-REQ372-20260921 -- verify with git branch --show-current, pull if needed.
acceptance_criteria: the empty-VariableSchema behavior is decided and stated explicitly, with reasoning
the amendment confirms (or corrects) compatibility with all 10 original acceptance criteria
no implementation code (function bodies) introduced -- signature/behavior description only

the fix, once implemented, must not require any of the ~31 pre-existing failing fixtures to be individually modified -- the amendment must work by construction, without editing unrelated test fixtures

result.summary: Amendment added as new S2.5 in lib/letflow/design/req372-semantic-decision-rule-validation.md. Decision: SemanticValidation.validate/2 skips both violation classes entirely and returns %{valid: true, violations: []} unconditionally when declared_fields == %{} (zero VariableSchema rows registered for the definition) -- option (a) from the triggering handoff. Reasoning: a process that never registered a schema has no schema to be wrong against; REQ-372 validates an existing schema, it does not mandate one exist; retroactively backfilling ~31 pre-existing fixtures (and real tenant data) is out of this requirement scope; the type-compatibility check already degrades to zero violations in this case via its existing :unresolvable exemption, so the only real gap was the field-existence check, now closed by this guard. The guard lives inside validate/2 itself (checked before any edge is walked), not at either call site, so both activate/2 (S3.2) and validate_definition_graph/2 (S3.3) get it uniformly by construction -- no call-site change needed. Compatibility with all 10 original ACs confirmed in writing in S2.5.4: AC1-AC6 all require a non-empty declared_fields by construction of their own test scenarios (a violation needs a declared set to be absent-from or type-incompatible-against), so the new empty-map branch is never reached by their test cases; AC7-AC9 are unrelated to declared_fields; AC10 is exactly what this amendment unblocks. No implementation code was written -- only @spec-level signature/behavior description was amended for validate/2 (unchanged @spec, one new documented behavior branch) and field_existence_violations/3 (signature and per-call behavior unchanged; amendment only prevents it from ever being invoked with an empty map).
